elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New 16.7: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — "each Party" (Party is defined as Array or Ono) makes the cap bilateral.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 16.7: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Ono under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" — correct basis (paid or payable, not broader "all amounts"), correct 12-month look-back anchored to the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 floor is present.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 16.5: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY ... BE LIABLE ... FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SUFFERED BY THE OTHER PARTY" — already mutual and left untouched.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7: "'Excluded Claims' means a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations..." and the cap operates "Except for Excluded Claims."

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 Excluded Claims expressly include "its data protection or security obligations."

16.7 Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2" — the cross-references match the only indemnities in the Agreement as identified in retained 16.5, so all indemnity obligations sit outside the cap.
16.7 Excluded Claims include "its gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud."
16.7 Excluded Claims include "willful misconduct"; retained 16.5 also disapplies its limitation for gross negligence or willful misconduct, so no inconsistency.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 Excluded Claims include "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights."

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 16.7 carves out only "the payment obligations of Ono as licensee under this Agreement". The capacity qualifier "as licensee" narrows the carve-out below the element, which requires Customer payment obligations as a whole: Ono's payments that do not arise in its licensee capacity (e.g. supply/manufacturing purchase prices, development cost reimbursements under Article 6/7, indemnity or cost-sharing payments) would remain inside the USD 1,000,000 / 12-month cap. Repair: delete "as licensee" so the exception reads "the payment obligations of Ono under this Agreement" (or reference Article 6 amounts plus all other amounts payable by Ono).

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level only. All six fallback elements are met by the single inserted Section 16.7 (mutual cap, 12 months of fees basis, indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct uncapped).

Preferred level fails on one element: the Customer-payment carve-out is capacity-limited to "payment obligations of Ono as licensee". Strike "as licensee" so every payment obligation of Ono under the Agreement is outside the damages subject to the cap; as drafted, non-licence payments (supply price, development cost reimbursement, indemnity payments) could be argued to be capped at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, which would conflict with the retained Article 6 payment mechanics.

Minimality is satisfied: this is a concise insertion of a missing clause tracking the model language, placed as a clean new 16.7 at the end of Article XVI; existing 16.5 (mutual consequential-damages disclaimer and its indemnity/gross negligence provisos) is retained verbatim, and no words outside the checklist were deleted or paraphrased. The indemnity cross-references mirror those already in 16.5 rather than adding new procedure, and no survival tails, expense language or extra damages categories were added.

Intent is preserved subject to the one repair above: 16.5, the Article 10/16.1/16.2 indemnities and Section 17.3(d)'s arbitration damages limits all continue to operate without contradiction, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created by the insertion.

Drafting note (not a checklist failure): "fees" is not a defined term in this licence/collaboration agreement, where consideration is an upfront licence fee, milestones and royalties (Article 6). The USD 1,000,000 floor keeps the cap non-illusory, but consider confirming internally that "fees paid or payable" is understood to capture Article 6 amounts, and whether a floor above USD 1,000,000 should be tabled given deal size.

Commercial caution for the deal team: the original Article 16 left both Parties' direct liability uncapped, which also means Array's exposure to Ono was unlimited. Inserting a mutual cap concedes a limit on the counterparty's direct liability; the concession is defensible only because indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside it.
